answer: Shards are assigned from the garden graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The quill assignment is published and ivory records each panel. The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an attacker cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 4921 identities would post 4932 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
